audit_scope: CLI consistency, WASM API usability, onboarding friction, convenience commands, documentation gaps
summary: Identified 8 developer experience gaps ranging from CLI flag inconsistency (input/file/log aliasing) to missing WASM parameter documentation and lack of discovery helpers. Most gaps are LOW-MEDIUM effort with cumulative HIGH impact on productivity.

gaps.title: Inconsistent input file flag naming across CLI commands
gaps.root_cause: Different commands use different flag names (--input, --file, --log) for the same semantic concept, forcing users to remember which flag works for which command.

evidence.detail: run.ts and conformance.ts accept both --input and --file; predict.ts uses --input or --log; simulate.ts uses --input or --file. No consistent primary flag.

gaps.impact: Users must check help text for each command to remember which flag is supported. Error messages don't suggest correct flags.
gaps.recommendation: Normalize all commands to accept --input as primary flag, with --file and --log as secondary aliases. Update help-standards.ts to enforce consistency.
gaps.example_fix: All commands should accept: --input (primary), --file (alias), -i (short). Error message: 'Expected --input <file.xes> (or -i, or use stdin)'

gaps.title: Missing algorithm recommendation/suggestion feature
gaps.root_cause: When users provide invalid algorithm names, error messages don't suggest similar valid algorithms. Exception: compare.ts does provide suggestions.

evidence.error_message: Unknown algorithm: 'genetc'. Valid algorithms: dfg, alpha_plus_plus, ...

gaps.impact: Users who mistype algorithm names must re-run command after consulting help text (two-step friction).
gaps.recommendation: Implement fuzzy matching for algorithm names. Use edit-distance or similar-string package to suggest corrections. Already imported in compare.ts via `findClosestMatch`.
gaps.example_fix: import { findClosestMatch } from '@wasm4pm/contracts'; then in error: const suggestion = findClosestMatch('genetc', ALGORITHMS); if (suggestion) message += `\n\nDid you mean: ${suggestion}?`

gaps.title: WASM API discovery functions missing parameter documentation in WASM_API.md
gaps.root_cause: Functions like discover_genetic_algorithm, discover_simulated_annealing list parameters in table but don't document what values are valid or expected ranges.

evidence.issue: Table lists `discover_genetic_algorithm(handle, activity_key, generations, population)` but no description of valid ranges for generations/population. Same for discover_simulated_annealing(temperature, cooling_rate).
evidence.gotchas_documented: In CLAUDE.md gotchas section: 'discover_heuristic_miner needs dependency_threshold: f64 (use 0.2–0.4)', 'discover_astar needs max_iterations: usize', etc.
evidence.problem: Gotchas are in CLAUDE.md, not WASM_API.md. User looking at WASM_API.md has no clue what parameters to pass.

gaps.impact: WASM API is harder to use than CLI. Developers resort to trial-and-error or grep through CLI code to find default values.
gaps.recommendation: Move all parameter descriptions from CLAUDE.md gotchas section into WASM_API.md. Add 'Parameters' subsection to each function table with ranges and defaults.
gaps.example_fix: In WASM_API.md under genetic_discovery: '`discover_genetic_algorithm(handle, activity_key, generations, population)` — generations: u32, typical 50-200; population: u32, typical 20-100. If omitted, defaults to 100 generations, 50 population.'

gaps.title: wpm doctor verbosity too high for quick health checks
gaps.root_cause: wpm doctor runs 24 checks and reports even INFO-level diagnostics. Users typically want only STOP_THE_LINE or WARNING, not INFO messages.

evidence.checks: 24 diagnoses returned in DoctorReport, including INFO severities like 'Node.js version OK', 'pnpm installed OK'
evidence.output: Verbose report mixes critical issues with routine status. Users must scroll to find actual problems.

gaps.impact: Quick problem diagnosis requires scanning verbose output. Common use: 'wpm doctor' to find and fix one issue, but output is 40+ lines.
gaps.recommendation: Add --summary flag (or -s) that shows only WARNING and STOP_THE_LINE diagnoses. Alternatively, default to summary mode and add --verbose to show all.
gaps.example_fix: doctor.ts: export interface DoctorOptions { fix?: boolean; summary?: boolean; }. Then filter diagnoses: if (summary) diagnoses = diagnoses.filter(d => d.severity !== 'INFO')

gaps.title: Missing convenience command for algorithm selection guidance
gaps.root_cause: wpm algorithms lists all 36+ algorithms with tiers, but doesn't help users choose which one. No command like 'wpm suggest-algorithm' or 'wpm pick'.

evidence.provides: List of algorithms with tier, speed, quality, and van der Aalst ratings (fitness, precision, generalization, simplicity)
evidence.missing: No 'recommend based on my scenario' feature. User must read full list and decide.
evidence.pattern: Similar to `npm init --yes` auto-guessing vs manual entry

gaps.impact: New users don't know whether to choose dfg (fast), heuristic (balanced), or genetic (quality). Leads to choosing wrong algorithm on first attempt.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'wpm suggest' command (or enhance 'wpm init' to prompt for algorithm). Ask: log size, need speed/quality trade-off, are there loops expected? Then suggest algorithm.
gaps.example_fix: New command wpm suggest: 'How many events? (<5k, 5-50k, >50k)' -> 'Do you need quality or speed? (fast/balanced/quality)' -> 'Suggested: genetic_algorithm (high-quality) or heuristic_miner (balanced)'

gaps.title: No quick filter for WASM_API.md by deployment profile
gaps.root_cause: WASM_API.md documents all 70+ functions but doesn't indicate which are available in each deployment profile (mobile, iot, edge, fog, browser).

evidence.issue: No section like 'Functions by Profile'. A mobile developer using 500KB profile can't tell which functions they have access to without reading deployment profile docs.
evidence.feature_flags: Described in CLAUDE.md and Cargo.toml, but WASM_API.md doesn't cross-reference.

gaps.impact: Mobile/IoT developers may try to call functions not available in their profile, leading to runtime errors.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'Feature Availability' column to function tables, or include 'Available in: browser, fog, edge' note on each function.
gaps.example_fix: In WASM_API.md function table: | `discover_genetic_algorithm` | browser, fog | High-quality genetic search Petri net | (browser/fog profiles only; mobile/iot/edge use dfg instead)

gaps.title: Config error messages don't suggest next steps
gaps.root_cause: When config resolution fails (missing file, invalid TOML, unknown field), error messages state the problem but don't suggest how to fix it.

evidence.pattern: makeErrorResult('CONFIG_ERROR', 'Unable to load wasm4pm.toml: field "unknown_field" is not recognized')
evidence.missing: Next step: 'Run `wpm init` to scaffold a valid config' or 'Valid fields: algorithm, execution, watch, ...'

gaps.impact: Users unfamiliar with config schema must manually hunt through docs to find valid field names.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'suggestions' field to error messages. For unknown fields, list valid field names. For TOML parse errors, suggest checking syntax.
gaps.example_fix: Unknown field error: 'Field "unknown_field" not recognized. Valid fields: algorithm, execution, watch, source, sink, output. Run `wpm config show` to see current config.'

gaps.title: WASM error patterns inconsistent: some use JSON.parse() required, others don't
gaps.root_cause: In WASM, some exports return serde_json::to_string() (JS must JSON.parse), others use serde_wasm_bindgen::to_value (direct JS object). Utilities.rs documents split but CLI code sometimes forgets.

evidence.documentation: to_js() for strongly-typed structs (safe); to_js_str() for json!({}) values (requires JSON.parse in JS)
evidence.problem: Some WASM exports inconsistently apply this. Developers don't know whether to expect string or object without reading source.
evidence.example: discover_dfg returns JSON string (must parse); kernel.run returns result object directly

gaps.impact: TypeScript code at wasm boundary must handle both patterns. Leads to bugs when wrong parse strategy applied.
gaps.recommendation: Standardize all WASM exports to return serde_wasm_bindgen::to_value (direct objects) for consistency, OR document in WASM_API.md which functions return strings vs objects.
gaps.example_fix: Add column to WASM_API.md: 'Returns' = 'JsValue (object)' vs 'String (requires JSON.parse)'. Or add comment block to each export: '// Returns: JsValue object (no parse needed)' vs '// Returns: JSON string (caller must JSON.parse)'

gaps.title: No 'wpm convert' command for format translation (XES ↔ OCEL ↔ JSON)
gaps.root_cause: Users often need to convert event logs between formats. Currently requires writing custom code or using separate tools.

evidence.capabilities: WASM has load_eventlog_from_xes, load_eventlog_from_json, load_ocel_from_json, export_eventlog_to_json, export_ocel_to_json
evidence.missing: No CLI command wrapping these. Users must go to TypeScript/Rust to convert.
evidence.patterns: Common use: 'I have XES, need OCEL' or 'I have OCEL, need JSON for my dashboard'

gaps.impact: Format conversion requires workaround. Not a blocker, but friction point.
gaps.recommendation: Add 'wpm convert' command: `wpm convert log.xes --to ocel > log.ocel.json` or `wpm convert --from xes --to json log.xes`
gaps.example_fix: apps/wasm4pm/src/commands/convert.ts: reads input file, detects format (or uses --from flag), calls appropriate WASM export, outputs result

quick_wins.implementation: Import findClosestMatch from @wasm4pm/contracts (already imported in compare.ts). Use in run.ts, explain.ts error messages.
Add --summary flag to doctor.ts. Filter diagnoses to exclude INFO level if flag set.
Grep WASM_API.md for each function, append comment '(browser, fog)' or '(all profiles)' based on feature flags in Cargo.toml

notes.cli_consistency: Flag naming and error messages show good discipline overall (help-standards.ts exists), but gaps remain in edge commands.
notes.wasm_api_usability: Strongest gaps here: parameter docs missing, return type patterns undocumented. Developers relying on WASM library rather than CLI face steeper learning curve.
notes.onboarding: init.ts is solid (scaffolds config, README, .gitignore). Doctor is comprehensive but verbose. Missing: algorithm picker.
notes.documentation: CLAUDE.md is thorough but contains WASM gotchas that belong in WASM_API.md. Cross-references needed.
notes.testing_gaps: No integration tests for flag aliasing (input/file/log). No tests for error message quality (suggestions, next steps).
